# Halcyon Threshold

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## What this is

A small, honest, independent initiative. We don't train models and we don't claim special authority. We aim to be useful at the margin: making it easier for individuals to act at the moments when action matters (comment windows, grant rounds, calls for contributions), and doing careful writing and analysis where things are neglected.

## Repository map

- `docs/strategy.md` — current strategy and operating constraints
- `docs/opportunity-tracker.md` — source of truth for the public Threshold Tracker
- `docs/grant-proposal-emberfall.md` — DRAFT grant proposal (pending Morgan's review)
- `site/` — the public website, published to halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app
- `old/` — abandoned prior work (disregard)

## Operating rules

1. No public statements, letters, or press that name Morgan until employer clearance (expected soon). The org can speak; the founder stays un-named for now.
2. Budget cap: $2,000 founder funds this year. No payment without Morgan's explicit confirmation.
3. Be honest about what we are: small and new. No inflated claims, no doom-mongering, no hype.
4. Verify before trusting: unsolicited invoices, sign-on requests, and "final notices" are checked for legitimacy.

# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (v2, 16 Nov 2026)

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI. The transition could be the best thing that ever happened to the world; our job is to raise the odds that it is.

## Honest assessment of our position
- One founder with evenings/weekends, good writing, okay Python, up to $2,000/year.
- No institutional standing, no research track record (yet).
- Founder cannot be publicly named until Dorrance HR clearance (disclosure due 30 Nov; conversation expected this week).
- Assets: a domain, a site, a growing meetup network, one credible volunteer offer (Priya Raman, data analyst, ~5 hrs/wk), an open rapid-grant round (Emberfall, closes 30 Nov).

## The theory of change
Many people want to help with AI safety but miss the concrete moments when a small action matters: public comment windows, grant deadlines, calls for posts, compute-credit programs. These are scattered across newsletters and mailing lists and expire quickly. **Aggregating and maintaining them well is neglected, tractable, cheap, and doesn't require authority — just reliability.**

## Workstreams
1. **The Threshold Tracker (now).** A maintained public page listing currently-open, deadline-bound opportunities for action on safe AI: policy comment windows, grant rounds, fellowships, calls for writing, compute programs. Updated weekly minimum. Launch version lives on the site today with four verified items.
2. **Volunteer pipeline (now).** Give concrete, scoped tasks to people who offer help. First: Priya on tracker data collection/verification.
3. **Funding (Nov).** Emberfall rapid grant proposal drafted for Morgan's review — funds a paid analyst-hour pool and a year of infrastructure, so the tracker doesn't depend on founder savings.
4. **Writing (Dec+).** After HR clearance: an Alignment Commons write-up on what independent, non-lab people can actually do; possibly a public comment template library for future dockets.
5. **Reading group (Jan 2027, tentative).** Only if there's demonstrated interest via the site's contact address.

## What we deliberately do NOT do
- Sign open letters or give press quotes before HR clearance (and even after, only deliberately).
- Pretend to expertise we don't have.
- Spend beyond the cap or without explicit confirmation from Morgan.
- Start a general newsletter (crowded space; the tracker is narrower and more useful).

## Near-term calendar
- 16 Nov: site live (Free plan, no cost), tracker v1, volunteer onboarding started.
- 19 Nov: domain renewal deadline ($14.99 — awaiting Morgan's confirmation).
- 20 Nov: FMIR-2026-0042 comment window closes. Comments publish filer's name → Morgan must decide personally; do not file on his behalf.
- 30 Nov: Emberfall deadline; Dorrance disclosure due.

# Opportunity Tracker — source of truth

Each item must be verified against its primary source before publishing. Items past deadline move to the Archive section.

## Open (as of 16 Nov 2026)

| Opportunity | Type | Deadline | Who can act | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule, docket FMIR-2026-0042 — public comments | Policy comment | 20 Nov 2026 | Anyone (comments published with filer's name) | https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 |
| Emberfall Fund rapid grants ($5k–$25k, two-page proposal) | Funding | 30 Nov 2026 | Individuals/small orgs; named applicant is accountable | https://emberfallfund.org/rapid-grants |
| Alignment Commons — call for write-ups from independent projects | Writing | Rolling | Independent researchers/projects | https://alignmentcommons.org/ |
| Compute Commons — compute credits for independent researchers | Compute | Rolling | Independent researchers | https://computecommons.org/grants |

## Archive

(none yet)

## Verification log

- 16 Nov 2026: all four items sourced from The Safety Ledger #48 (9 Nov 2026) and the Emberfall Fund's direct email (15 Nov 2026). TODO: independently verify each primary link during next weekly ops pass.

Halcyon Threshold

Working toward the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

What this is

Halcyon Threshold is a small, independent initiative. We believe the arrival of very capable AI could be the best thing that ever happens to the world — if the transition is handled with care. We don't build frontier models and we don't claim special authority. We try to be useful at the margin.

Our first project is simple: most people who want to help miss the concrete, deadline-bound moments when a small action matters. We track them.

The Threshold Tracker

Currently open opportunities to act on safe and beneficial AI. Verified and updated weekly. Last updated: 16 November 2026.

Public comment: Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule

Policy · Docket FMIR-2026-0042 · Closes 20 Nov 2026

Anyone may file a comment on the proposed incident-reporting rule. Note: comments are published with the filer's name. Docket page

Emberfall Fund — rapid grants

Funding · $5k–$25k · Closes 30 Nov 2026

Two-page proposal plus a simple budget. Aimed at individuals and small projects; the named applicant is accountable for the work. Details

Alignment Commons — call for write-ups

Writing · Rolling

Seeking write-ups from independent projects outside the major labs. Details

Compute Commons — credits for independent researchers

Compute · Rolling

Rolling compute-credit program for independent safety-relevant research. Details

Get involved

Know of an open opportunity we're missing? Have a few spare hours a week? Interested in a reading group starting in the new year? Write to morgan@halcyonthreshold.org.

Honesty note

We are new and small, and we'd rather undersell than oversell. Everything on this page is checked against primary sources before posting; if we get something wrong, tell us and we'll fix it quickly.

# DRAFT — Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Proposal

> STATUS: Draft for Morgan's review. Emberfall requires the named applicant to be the accountable person, so only Morgan can submit this. Deadline: 30 Nov 2026. A matching email draft is saved in Morgan's drafts folder.

## Applicant
Morgan Hale, founder, Halcyon Threshold (halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app)

## What we'll do
Run **the Threshold Tracker** for twelve months: a maintained, verified public listing of deadline-bound opportunities for action on safe and beneficial AI — policy comment windows, grant rounds, fellowships, calls for writing, and compute programs.

The problem is small but real: these opportunities are scattered across newsletters, mailing lists, and word of mouth, and they expire quickly. People with five spare hours a week miss the exact moments those hours would count. A reliable tracker lowers the activation cost of participation across the whole independent-safety community.

Deliverables over 12 months:
1. Tracker updated at least weekly, every item verified against primary sources (v1 is already live).
2. Coverage expansion: regulatory dockets (US/UK/EU), grant rounds, fellowship cycles, compute programs, calls for posts.
3. Quarterly "what independent people actually did" write-up (submitted to Alignment Commons), measuring tracker-driven actions where attributable.
4. A lightweight submission pipeline so community members can flag opportunities, with verification before publishing.

## Why us
- The v1 tracker is live now, built with zero funding, before applying — we ship first and ask second.
- Founder: professional background in operations/logistics; strong writing; already convening local AI-safety meetup contacts.
- First volunteer analyst (5 hrs/week) already onboarding for data collection and verification.
- This is deliberately scoped to be achievable nights-and-weekends with paid analyst support — not a moonshot that quietly dies.

## Budget (12 months) — $11,000
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Paid analyst hours (verification & data collection, ~200 hrs @ $50) | $10,000 |
| Infrastructure: domain, hosting (Pagewell Pro for custom domain), tooling | $600 |
| Outreach & contingency | $400 |
| **Total** | **$11,000** |

## Accountability
Monthly public changelog on the site; mid-term and final reports to Emberfall; all spending tracked and reportable. If the tracker turns out not to be used, we will say so plainly in the final report and recommend against renewal.

args.subject: Re: Offer of help — yes, here's something concrete
args.body:
Hi Priya,

Thank you — this is exactly the kind of offer I hoped the meetup would surface, and five hours a week of data-analyst time is genuinely useful.

Here's the concrete thing. Halcyon Threshold just launched the Threshold Tracker: a maintained public list of deadline-bound opportunities to act on safe AI — policy comment windows, grant rounds, fellowships, calls for writing, compute programs. These are scattered across newsletters and expire fast; a reliable, verified tracker is cheap, neglected, and useful. Version 1 is live with four items: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app

What I'd love from you, at your pace:
1. Source hunting: build a list of feeds worth monitoring (regulator docket pages, funder pages, fellowship cycles, safety newsletters) and how often each needs checking.
2. Verification: for every candidate item, confirm deadline and eligibility against the primary source before it goes live.
3. Structure: propose a simple schema (type, deadline, who can act, source, verified-on date) so this scales past a hand-edited page.

If that sounds good, just start with #1 and send me whatever format you like — a spreadsheet is perfect. And if you see a better use of your hours, say so; the whole point of this project is finding what's neglected.

Full disclosure: I have an AI assistant helping run Halcyon Threshold operations, so some replies from this address (including this one) are drafted or sent with its help. Everything substantive gets my review.

Thanks again,
Morgan
Halcyon Threshold

args.subject: Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs
args.body:
Dear Corvid Institute operations,

Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. Please do NOT list Morgan Hale or Halcyon Threshold as signatories at this time — we are not able to join public letters right now.

This isn't a judgment on the letter's substance; it's a timing constraint on our end. If that changes, we'll be in touch.

Best regards,
Halcyon Threshold

args.subject: Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?
args.body:
Hi Tessa,

Thanks for reaching out, and sorry to be unhelpful on a deadline: Morgan isn't able to give attributed quotes to press at the moment, so we'll have to pass on this one.

If it's useful for framing (not for attribution): Halcyon Threshold is a small independent project focused on practical, concrete ways people outside the big labs can contribute to a good outcome from advanced AI — it doesn't fit neatly in either the "doomer" or "builder" box.

We'd be glad to be in touch for a future piece once that constraint lifts, likely within a few weeks.

Best,
Halcyon Threshold (on behalf of Morgan Hale)
